parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the prompt requirements to implement std-only Rust 2021, parse args through std::env::args, place test5.rs and Cargo project files under /output, and match the observable output of the C++ binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept an implementation plan for itself while also spawning a probe child. The child then spawned a grandchild for black-box probing and independently took on implementation work in the same /output workspace.
parallel.implementation: The parent first wrote Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/clipper2lib modules, and test5.rs. The child later wrote a different Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/clipper2 modules, and test5.rs; the final tree contained both module families, with the root entrypoint pointing at the child-style src/clipper2 module.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened through shared /output side effects rather than an explicit merge protocol. The parent noticed that Cargo.toml and test5.rs no longer matched its prior files, inspected the changed tree, and delivered the mixed workspace.
parallel.verification: The parent built and ran its initial implementation with rustc and Cargo, then the child built and compared its own implementation against the C++ binary. The official evaluator later passed 1/1 testcase.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The task output passed, but the parallel process left a provenance problem: a child overwrote the parent-owned deliverable/source tree and the child was interrupted before a normal parent-facing final handoff.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, CLI, project structure, and byte-for-byte stdout requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the whole pipeline: inspect the source and executable, design a small Clipper-style API, write the Cargo package and root test5.rs, compile, verify, and deliver.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote Cargo.toml, /output/test5.rs, and a /output/clipper2 module tree implementing Point64, Path64, Paths64, FillRule, and the four boolean operation functions used by the test.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation was assembled in one coherent tree with no cross-agent merge or workspace overwrite. It produced /output/test5 and /output/target/release/test5.
serial.verification: The serial actor built successfully with rustc and Cargo, ran the Rust binaries, and compared no-arg and extra-arg stdout against /workspace/dataset/test5_executable with cmp returning 0.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation is visible in the trajectory; the official evaluator completed and passed 1/1 testcase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required Rust project structure, std-only constraint, root test5.rs, CLI collection, and exact output behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and implemented the same observable behavior from the same source and binary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference explains the outcome; both passed. The difference is in process coordination, not task understanding.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a parent implementation plan plus a probe child; the child in turn spawned a grandchild and then independently wrote an implementation in the same output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one owner for investigation, implementation, build, verification, and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel duplicated implementation ownership across parent and child, while serial kept a single coherent owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The visible parallel interface gave the child a probe-oriented path/name, but the child worked in the same /output implementation surface; no separate file ownership contract is visible before the shared writes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent interface boundary and controlled all file/module decisions locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a coordination boundary around shared /output writes; serial avoided that boundary entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented a clipper2lib module tree and root test5.rs, then the child implemented a separate src/clipper2 module tree and rewrote the root test5.rs to use it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented one /output/clipper2 module tree and root test5.rs without another actor replacing it.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementations passed, but parallel changed implementation path mid-run because a child wrote a competing tree after the parent implementation already existed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited twice for the child, saw available child/probe information through agent listing, sent a message, then interrupted the child rather than receiving a normal final handoff from that child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and proceeded directly from local verification to final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a messy child-result lifecycle, but the final solution came from shared files and local inspection rather than from a clean returned child result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A child wrote over the parent-owned root deliverable/config path and added a competing source tree in /output, after which the parent noticed unexpected changes and inspected the mixed file set.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and delivered a single consistent project tree without cross-agent workspace mutation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material coordination difference: parallel had a concrete shared-state overwrite episode; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent and child both ran successful builds and output checks at different times, and the official evaluator passed the final artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built with rustc and Cargo, ran the generated binaries, compared stdout to the C++ executable for no args and extra args, and the official evaluator passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was coherent within one implementation. Parallel verification was split across parent and child implementations, but still ended in an official pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more time, requests, tool calls, and three subagents; it still completed within budget and passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one rollout, fewer requests and tool calls, completed sooner, and passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred extra coordination overhead and cleanup/inspection but did not run out of budget or fail closure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are concordant: parallel and serial both passed 1 of 1 testcase. Serial solved the task through one coherent implementation path. Parallel also solved it, but the final workspace passed despite a concrete child-over-parent overwrite of /output/test5.rs and related build/source files. Therefore the retained concurrency pattern describes an adverse parallel process consequence, not a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parent independently implemented and verified a Rust solution before the child changed the output tree.
Child implementation in the shared /output workspace replaced the root deliverable/source configuration but also built and matched the required observable output.
Parent inspected the changed final tree before finalizing.
serial_contributors: Single actor maintained one implementation tree from creation through build and output comparison.
Serial verification compared generated stdout against the C++ executable with no args and extra args.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial tree used /output/clipper2 modules, while the final parallel tree used /output/src/clipper2 plus leftover parent /output/src/clipper2lib files.
Both implementations approximated only the rectangle boolean behavior needed by this test, which was sufficient for the official testcase.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a directly evidenced adverse parallel process episode
